samples.summary: Turning the offline toggle off erases the disk, but the still-mounted durable client immediately re-writes every open document back to it
samples.evidence: `watchForOfflineDisable` (offline-erase.ts:346) calls `eraseOfflineData` → `WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser`, which `purge()`s every key **and** adds each to `this.evicted` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:963-970). By deliberate design (`collab-document-provider.tsx:204-228`, `use-durable-document.ts:134-164`) the durable client is NOT torn down when the preference flips — it stays mounted for the life of the open document. Its next `appendChange` finds no header, hits `refuseIfEvicted` and throws (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:608-610, 665-674); the store's own doc-comment states the purpose of that throw is to make the SDK "poison the log and write a fresh snapshot". That fresh `saveSnapshot` re-creates the snapshot/header rows and clears the evicted mark (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:549-554). Net effect: seconds after the user switches the setting off, the document they had open is back on disk, and no further preference change will ever fire to remove it (the listener only acts on a true→false edge). The Settings copy that promises "turning it off deletes what was stored" is therefore false for exactly the document the user was looking at. Nothing in the erase path detaches, disables, or stops the live store.

samples.summary: The owed-erase marker is a single localStorage slot that any later sign-out clears or overwrites, so one account's documents can be left on a shared device forever
samples.evidence: `PENDING_ERASE_KEY` holds at most one user id. In `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` both success branches call `rememberPendingErase(undefined)` unconditionally (offline-erase.ts:169 and 172) — they do not check that the recorded owed id is the user this erase was for. Sequence: user A signs out, the IndexedDB erase throws, `rememberPendingErase("A")` (line 178). User B signs in; `retryPendingOfflineErase` also fails (it swallows and keeps the marker, line 208-210). B's session expires → `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm calls `logout({eraseLocalData:"keep-archives"})` → B's erase succeeds → `rememberPendingErase(undefined)` wipes the marker that named **A**. A's live entries and archives stay on the disk with nothing left that can name them. The same single slot also means a second failing logout (`rememberPendingErase(who)`) silently overwrites a still-owed erase for a different account.

samples.summary: The session reconcile purges any stored document missing from a listing it fetched earlier, racing documents another tab created or has open
samples.evidence: `OfflineRuntime` fetches `fetchDocuments()` (offline-runtime.tsx:114) and then `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments(...)` deletes every stored document id **not** in that list, with `archives: "drop"` (offline-erase.ts:281-286). The IndexedDB database is shared across tabs and `storedDocumentIds()` is scoped only by user, so it includes entries written by *another tab of the same user*. A document created (or first persisted) in tab A after tab B's `/documents` response returns is absent from B's list and present in B's store scan, so B purges it. `WafflebaseDocStore.purge` (line 781) — unlike `dropAllForUser` — neither consults `isLive`/`isOpenElsewhere` nor adds the key to `evicted`, so tab A's subsequent `appendChange` finds no header, returns the contract's silent "no base" success, and every later edit goes nowhere while tab A's chip still reports `saved-locally`. That is precisely the silent-loss failure the eviction and collection paths go to lengths to avoid; this path has none of those guards.

samples.summary: The durable provider's WafflebaseDocStore is never closed, leaking an IndexedDB connection per document open
samples.evidence: `const store = useMemo(() => new WafflebaseDocStore({...}), [userId])` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:113-125) has no accompanying `useEffect` cleanup calling `store.close()`, and no other code path closes it. Every other creator of a store in this change closes it (`offline-erase.ts:180, 211, 244, 292`; `offline-runtime.tsx:143`). Each durable document open therefore leaves an open `IDBDatabase` handle for the tab's lifetime; a changed `userId` replaces the memo without closing the previous one. Open connections block `deleteDatabase`/version upgrades (only partially mitigated by the `onversionchange` handler at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:434).

samples.summary: `lost` and `writesFailing` latches are never reset when the provider's document changes, so a later document is reported non-durable because an earlier one failed
samples.evidence: `const [lost, setLost] = useState(false)` (line 91) and `const [writesFailing, setWritesFailing] = useState(false)` (line 112) are deliberately latched, but they are keyed to nothing — not `clientKey`, not the document. `DurableYorkieProvider` is rendered at a fixed position in `CollabDocumentProvider` and only its `clientKey` prop changes when the same mounted provider moves to another document, so a loss or write failure reported for document A keeps `durable=false` for document B for the rest of the provider's life. The chip then shows `not-saved` for work that is in fact on disk. (Safe direction, but wrong: the doc-comment claims the store is "created once per client key" while the memo deps are `[userId]`, so the mismatch is not intentional.)

samples.summary: The fallback store created inside the preference-change listener is never closed
samples.evidence: `const current = store() ?? new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId: who });` (offline-erase.ts:338) — when the fallback branch is taken (the documented common case: Settings is its own route, so no editor store exists) the newly constructed store opens a database connection and nothing ever calls `close()` on it. The `void eraseOfflineData(current, who).catch(...)` on line 346 has no `finally { current.close(); }`, unlike every other store-creating function in this file.

samples.summary: A network failure on the logout request skips the local erase entirely and records nothing to retry
samples.evidence: In `logout()` the `fetch` is wrapped in a try that rethrows when `!suppressFailure` (auth.ts:106-110), which happens **before** `await eraseOfflineDataOnLogout(...)` on line 125. So a deliberate sign-out attempted while offline or against an unreachable backend throws out of `logout` without erasing anything and without calling `rememberPendingErase`, leaving the device's stored documents in place with no owed-erase marker for the next session to finish.

samples.summary: `purgeOfflineDocuments` abandons the remaining ids when one purge throws
samples.evidence: The `for (const id of documentIds)` loop (offline-erase.ts:236-240) sits inside a single `try`/`catch`. A failure on the first id skips every remaining id in the batch, so `deleteDocuments` with several ids can leave most of the deleted documents' content on disk while logging a single warning. Iterating with a per-id try/catch would make the best-effort promise the doc-comment makes actually hold.

samples.summary: Accepting the offline offer immediately re-schedules and re-shows the 'Not saved' warning toast
samples.evidence: The warning effect now depends on `offerOffline` and `turnOnOfflineSaving` (sync-status-chip.tsx:265). Clicking the action sets the preference, flipping `offlineEnabled` true and therefore `offerOffline` false (line 146); the effect re-runs, the cleanup clears the pending timer, and — because `stranded` is still true — a **new** 2s timer fires `toast.warning('Not saved', {id: TOAST_ID})` again. The user who just acted on the offer sees the destructive warning reappear on top of the success toast they were given.

samples.summary: `use-durable-document.ts` is recorded as a binary file in the diff, so its contents were not reviewable in the change
samples.evidence: The diff shows `Binary files /dev/null and packages/frontend/src/lib/use-durable-document.ts differ` instead of the file's contents. The most likely cause is a literal NUL byte in the source — line 179 builds `const subject = `${eligible}�${userId ?? ""}�${docKey}`;`. It is functionally harmless but it hides a core policy module from every diff, review tool and blame view; a printable separator (e.g. `` written as an escape, or `|`) would keep the file text.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `watchForOfflineDisable` (offline-erase.ts:305-350) erases via `dropAllForUser`, which purges each key and marks it evicted (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:963-970) without touching any live store — the store class has no disable/stop state (only `close()` at 452) and no write path consults the preference (grep for getOfflinePersistenceEnabled: no hits in the store). The durable client is deliberately kept mounted across a preference flip (use-durable-document.ts:134-164 latch "may rise ... never fall"; collab-document-provider.tsx:204-248 holds the election per open). The next `appendChange` finds no header and `refuseIfEvicted` throws (575-614, 665-674), whose documented purpose (569-573) is to make the SDK write a fresh snapshot; `saveSnapshot` (537-556) unconditionally re-puts the snapshot+header and clears the evicted mark. The disable edge reaches tabs with open editors because the subscription covers cross-tab `storage` events (offline-persistence-preference.ts:102-109) and OfflineRuntime mounts the watcher in every authenticated tab (offline-runtime.tsx:54-74); the store's own comment at 169-167 concedes the other-tab case ends with "the SDK repairs the base". Since the listener only acts on the true→false edge (offline-erase.ts:322), no later change re-erases. Real, reachable, and a broken invariant/incorrect persisted state in the correctness lane.

finding.evidence: `PENDING_ERASE_KEY` holds at most one user id. In `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` both success branches call `rememberPendingErase(undefined)` unconditionally (offline-erase.ts:169 and 172) — they do not check that the recorded owed id is the user this erase was for. Sequence: user A signs out, the IndexedDB erase throws, `rememberPendingErase("A")` (line 178). User B signs in; `retryPendingOfflineErase` also fails (it swallows and keeps the marker, line 208-210). B's session expires → `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm calls `logout({eraseLocalData:"keep-archives"})` → B's erase succeeds → `rememberPendingErase(undefined)` wipes the marker that named **A**. A's live entries and archives stay on the disk with nothing left that can name them. The same single slot also means a second failing logout (`rememberPendingErase(who)`) silently overwrites a still-owed erase for a different account.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. PENDING_ERASE_KEY (offline-erase.ts:115) is a single localStorage slot holding at most one user id, and it is used nowhere else in the repo. Both success branches of eraseOfflineDataOnLogout call rememberPendingErase(undefined) (lines 169 and 172) without comparing the erasing user `who` (line 153) to the id currently recorded in the slot, and the failure path (line 178) overwrites any still-owed id. retryPendingOfflineErase swallows failures and keeps the marker (lines 208-210), so an owed erase for user A can survive into user B's session. Reachability is concrete: offline-runtime.tsx:57 re-records the signed-in identity as B on mount, offline-runtime.tsx:84 runs the retry (which may fail), and api/auth.ts:125-127 runs eraseOfflineDataOnLogout on every logout including the 401/keep-archives path, whose success then clears A's marker. Since dropAllForUser is user-scoped (offline-erase.ts:31), B's erase does not touch A's data, and no guard, reconciliation, or per-user marker exists anywhere to recover it. This is a broken invariant plus silent overwrite of persisted recovery state — correctness lane, major impact.

finding.evidence: `OfflineRuntime` fetches `fetchDocuments()` (offline-runtime.tsx:114) and then `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments(...)` deletes every stored document id **not** in that list, with `archives: "drop"` (offline-erase.ts:281-286). The IndexedDB database is shared across tabs and `storedDocumentIds()` is scoped only by user, so it includes entries written by *another tab of the same user*. A document created (or first persisted) in tab A after tab B's `/documents` response returns is absent from B's list and present in B's store scan, so B purges it. `WafflebaseDocStore.purge` (line 781) — unlike `dropAllForUser` — neither consults `isLive`/`isOpenElsewhere` nor adds the key to `evicted`, so tab A's subsequent `appendChange` finds no header, returns the contract's silent "no base" success, and every later edit goes nowhere while tab A's chip still reports `saved-locally`. That is precisely the silent-loss failure the eviction and collection paths go to lengths to avoid; this path has none of those guards.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element checks out. offline-runtime.tsx:114-116 fetches the listing and calls purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments; offline-erase.ts:278-286 opens a store WITHOUT the isOpenElsewhere callback (which the runtime's own store at offline-runtime.tsx:59-66 passes precisely to avoid purging a doc another tab has open) and purges every stored id absent from the list with archives:"drop". storedDocumentIds (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:843-855) is scoped only by user on the shared IndexedDB, so it includes entries written by other tabs of the same user. purgeDocument -> purge (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:813-829, 781-789) neither consults isLive/isOpenElsewhere (unlike collectStale:1026 and evictOldest:1273) nor adds the key to evicted (unlike dropAllForUser:948-971, whose comment states the marking exists exactly to prevent silent vanishing appends). appendChange (575-613) with no header returns a silent success because refuseIfEvicted (665-674) only throws for evicted keys, and the evicted set is per-tab module state (169-176, 323-325) with no cross-tab broadcast (no BroadcastChannel anywhere in frontend/src). Reachable: /documents (document.controller.ts:180-195) reflects server state at query time and lists only workspace-member docs, so a doc created in tab A after tab B's query, or one deleted/revoked while tab A has it open, is absent from B's list and present in B's scan -> B purges it and A's later edits silently go nowhere while the chip reports saved-locally. Silent local data loss on a reachable path; correctness lane (missing guard / data loss).

finding.summary: The durable client outlives the election it depends on: the decision is latched in `held.current` but `useDurableDocument` releases the Web Lock when the preference flips off
finding.evidence: `held.current` is written once per `subject` (line 242-244) and deliberately never re-read from `durable`, so the `DurableYorkieProvider` with `clientKey = wb:{userId}:{docKey}` and the store stays mounted for the life of the open document. But `useDurableDocument`'s effect (use-durable-document.ts:152-181) has `eligible` in its dependency list, so when `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` flips to false the cleanup runs and calls `handle.release()` — freeing `wb-durable:{userId}:{docKey}` while this tab is still writing under the stable client key. Both halves are pinned by tests: use-durable-document.test.tsx 'gives the election back when it is switched off' asserts `locks.held.size === 0`, and collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx 'keeps its client when the preference changes underneath it' asserts the durable clientKey is still mounted. If the preference is then turned back on and the same document is opened in a second tab, that tab wins the now-free election and mounts a client with the *identical* stable key — the shared-actor / colliding-clientSeq case the whole election exists to prevent (durable-session.ts:11-24), i.e. silent edit loss. Even without a second tab, the tab keeps writing document content to disk after the user switched local saving off.

verdict.reason: The finding's mechanism does not exist in the code. It claims the effect's `eligible` dependency lets eligibility fall when the offline-persistence preference flips off, running cleanup and releasing the Web Lock under a still-mounted durable client. But `eligible` is not the live value: `use-durable-document.ts:127-132` computes `eligibleNow`, and lines 157-164 latch it in a ref keyed on `identity = ${userId} ${docKey}`. The only two mutations are re-latching when identity changes (159-160) and rising false->true (161-162); there is no arm that lowers it. So on a preference flip with the same user and doc, `eligible` stays true, `subject` (line 179) is unchanged, and the effect deps `[eligible, userId, docKey, subject]` (line 214) do not change — the cleanup at 210-213 never runs and `handle.release()` is not called. The comment at 134-156 documents this latch as the deliberate fix for precisely the scenario described. The reviewer's cited test does not exist as quoted: the actual test is `use-durable-document.test.tsx:172-196` "keeps the election it already holds when it is switched off", which after `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled(false)` asserts `durable === true` AND `locks.held.size === 1` (194-195); release occurs only on unmount (198-214). The companion provider test (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:294-314) pins the same, consistent behavior. With the lock never freed, the claimed second-tab collision on the stable client key (durable-session.ts:11-24) has no trigger. The residual "keeps writing to disk after the preference is off" is the documented per-open latch (use-durable-document.ts:147-151, collab-document-provider.tsx:204-228) with an accompanying erase, i.e. a product decision, not a logic defect in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: `dropAllForUser` records the `evicted` marker on the erasing store instance, which is never the instance the durable client writes through — so post-erase appends are silently ignored while the chip still reports `saved-locally`
finding.evidence: `dropAllForUser` purges each key and then does `this.evicted.add(docKey)` (line 858-862) so that a later `appendChange` throws instead of being silently ignored (`refuseIfEvicted`, line 617-626, reading `this.evicted`, a per-instance `Set` declared line ~/`private readonly evicted`). But `evicted` is per-instance and the erase never runs on the instance the SDK holds: `watchForOfflineDisable` is handed `() => store` from OfflineRuntime's own `new WafflebaseDocStore(...)` (offline-runtime.tsx:55-70), and `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` constructs a throwaway `new WafflebaseDocStore({userId: who})` (offline-erase.ts:123), while the live client writes through the store created in `DurableYorkieProvider` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:86-97). That instance's `evicted` set stays empty, so its `appendChange` takes the `!header` branch (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:540-541, 560-563) and resolves successfully with nothing written, while `useDocumentDurability()` still answers true and the chip keeps showing 'Saved to this device'. Worse on the logout path: the next `saveSnapshot` from the still-mounted client re-creates the just-erased entry, putting the signed-out user's document content back on disk after the erase logout promised.

verdict.reason: The finding's central mechanism is not present in the code. `evicted` is not a per-instance Set: wafflebase-doc-store.ts:169-178 declares a module-level `const evictedKeys = new Map<string, Set<string>>()` with `evictedFor(dbName)`, and wafflebase-doc-store.ts:323-325 defines `private get evicted() { return evictedFor(this.dbName); }` — a getter into that shared map, not the `private readonly evicted` field the finding quotes. The comment at :153-168 documents the per-instance version as a bug that was deliberately replaced for exactly the reason the reviewer gives. Every production construction uses the default database name (`:343` `options.dbName ?? DEFAULT_DB_NAME`; no `dbName` passed at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:115-123, offline-runtime.tsx:59-66, or offline-erase.ts:158 — a repo-wide grep shows `dbName` is only ever supplied in *.test.ts files), so the erasing instance and the instance the SDK writes through resolve to the same Set. The marker added by dropAllForUser (:970) is therefore the one refuseIfEvicted reads (:666) on the durable client's instance, and appendChange (:608-611) throws as designed rather than silently succeeding. Both downstream consequences claimed (chip still reporting saved-locally, and an unmarked entry being re-created by the next saveSnapshot) depend on that false premise. The only residual the code actually concedes is cross-tab (:164-167), which is a different and explicitly bounded case.

finding.summary: `documentIdsIn` filters on `document.workspaceId` using what the call site passes as the workspace *slug*, so the workspace-delete purge silently matches nothing
finding.evidence: `deleteWorkspace(id)` is called as `deleteWorkspace(workspaceId!)` from the `/w/:workspaceId/settings` route param (workspace-settings.tsx:182), and that param is a slug — the same file navigates with `/w/${updated.slug}/settings` (line 103) and `/w/${remaining[0].slug}` (line 189). `documentIdsIn` then compares that slug to `document.workspaceId` (workspaces.ts:98), which is the document's workspace **id** (types/documents.ts:41, populated from the backend's `workspaceId` column). The filter therefore yields `[]` for every real deletion, `purgeOfflineDocuments([])` returns immediately (offline-erase.ts:148), and the local copies of a deleted workspace's documents stay on disk until the thirty-day sweep — exactly the outcome this code was added to prevent. The same mismatch applies to `removeMember`'s `documentIdsIn(workspaceId)` (line 138). Nothing fails loudly, so the no-op is invisible.

verdict.reason: The finding describes `documentIdsIn` as a bare `document.workspaceId === ref` comparison that matches nothing when `ref` is a slug. That code is not present. The actual implementation (packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:101-115) resolves the reference first via `fetchWorkspace(ref)` and filters on `document.workspaceId === ref || (!!workspace && document.workspaceId === workspace.id)`, accepting id and slug alike. The cited "line 98" is inside the doc comment (lines 95-99), which narrates the slug/id mismatch as a previously-fixed bug, not as live code. The resolution step genuinely works with a slug: workspace.controller.ts:39-44 routes GET workspaces/:id to findOne, and workspace.service.ts:53-68 tests the param against a UUID regex and looks up `where: isUUID ? { id } : { slug }`, returning the full record including `id`; workspace.service.spec.ts:162-176 asserts this slug lookup explicitly. So for deleteWorkspace(workspaceId!) at workspace-settings.tsx:182 with a slug route param, fetchWorkspace succeeds, workspace.id is the real id, documents match, and purgeOfflineDocuments receives a populated list rather than []. The same holds for removeMember's documentIdsIn(workspaceId) at workspaces.ts:160.

searchedFor: read wafflebase-doc-store.ts error paths (withQuotaRetry, refuseIfEvicted, appendChange, saveMeta)
finding.summary: Nothing lowers `durable` when the store fails or refuses its writes, so the chip can promise `saved-locally` for work that is not on disk
finding.evidence: `SyncSignals.durable` is documented as the conjunction of three facts, one of which is 'the store is not failing its writes' (sync-status/sync-state.ts:40-48). The only thing that ever lowers it is `reportLoss`, latched solely from the SDK's `local-changes-dropped` event (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:104-105, 160-163). A store write that rejects — `withQuotaRetry` giving up after one eviction (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1081-1084), `refuseIfEvicted` throwing, or `open()` rejecting because IndexedDB is unavailable — never reaches `reportLoss`, and neither does the silent `!header` no-op path. `useDocumentDurability()` therefore keeps answering true and `deriveSyncState` keeps returning `saved-locally`, i.e. the chip tells the user their unsent work survives a reload when it is not on disk. This is the one direction the design says the feature must not fail in.

verdict.reason: The finding claims nothing lowers `durable` when the store fails or refuses its writes, leaving reportLoss/local-changes-dropped as the sole lowering path. The code contradicts this. durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:112 holds a `writesFailing` latch, :122 passes `onWriteFailure: () => setWritesFailing(true)` into the WafflebaseDocStore constructor, and :128 computes `durable: !lost && !writesFailing` — a second, independent lowering input. The store honours it: options.onWriteFailure is captured at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:340/347 and `reportWriteFailure` (:1226-1232) fires on every branch where withQuotaRetry gives up — non-quota failure (:1205), nothing idle left to evict (:1208-1211), and the post-eviction retry failing (:1213-1217). Each path the finding names reaches it: refuseIfEvicted (:665-669) throws inside the wrapped op at :609 and :649, and open() is called inside the op (:540, :581, :627), so an unavailable IndexedDB rejects into the same catch; appendChange/saveMeta/saveSnapshot are all wrapped (:539, :580, :626). The latch never resets and is test-pinned (durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:60-82; wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:582,606,625). The finding's cited line numbers (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1081-1084) do not correspond to this tree. Only a far narrower residual remains — the `!header` no-op when the key is not in the `evicted` set returns silently (:588-590 with :608-611, :636-638 with :645-651) — which is a different, much smaller claim and does not sustain the one raised.
